answer: Price new identities with a self-adjusting base fee. The ledger targets, say, twenty registrations per epoch, and each epoch the burned join fee rises 12% if more joined than the target and falls 12% if fewer did. Honest arrivals trickle in and pay a stable price. A farm that tries to mint a thousand names drives the fee up exponentially within a few epochs, so each extra vertex in its graph costs more than the last, and spreading the attack slowly only buys at the normal rate. The fee is burned, not paid to anyone, so no walnut-sized bribe or pigment of insider favour can rebate it.
